name: Math function precision
plain: Evaluates Math.tan, cosh, expm1 and similar at odd inputs and compares the exact digits.
meaning: JS engines and CPU math libraries round the last bits differently, so a few results separate V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore and sometimes the OS and CPU architecture.

steps: Evaluate a short list of Math calls

limits.headline: Can run maths tests and use the last digits to tell your browser and chip apart
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Compute a few unusual maths results
Tell Chrome, Firefox and Safari engines apart by tiny digit differences
Sometimes guess your system and chip type
cannot: See your files or what you typed
Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: A script calculates unusual math functions and compares exact digits, which differ slightly by engine and CPU.
story.for_you: You see nothing. Your device does a few odd math problems and the tail digits can differ between browsers and chips. The answer helps identify your browser engine and system.
story.for_makers: Math answers are meant to be the same everywhere, but tiny rounding differences exist. Fraud and bot teams use them to tell real browsers from fake ones, and trackers add them to device IDs.

use_cases.example: A bot detector runs math tests and sees results that do not match the browser it claims to be.
A fingerprint library adds the exact digits from a few math calls to a visitor ID.
A physics heavy browser game makes sure players on different devices get the same results, so it avoids relying on risky math.
An ad script uses math results to separate browser engines when the user agent string is hidden.
A bank checks that the browser's math matches known real devices, to spot an emulator.
A web 3D tool runs on many chips and tests that its math gives matching shapes.
A web calculator or graphing site like Desmos shows the same answer on every device by controlling how it rounds.

risks: Hard to change without breaking math

technical_bounds: Same engine and CPU yield the same values, low per-user entropy

value.abuse: Browser and architecture identification inside composite hashes

history.change: Mulazzani et al. JS engine fingerprinting by conformance and speed
